# ARC Region Coloring

Use this procedure when demonstrations show thin color-1 outlines, color-2 exterior accents, and color-3 interior accents. Do not assume it applies to unrelated ARC tasks.

1. Copy the grid exactly and identify zero regions with 4-neighbor connectivity. Flood from every zero on the grid edge to mark exterior zeros; all other zero components are enclosed.
2. Find 4-connected components of color 1. Only components adjacent (in 4-neighbor terms) to at least one enclosed zero region are eligible; leave all other components and their surroundings unchanged. If none qualify, return the grid unchanged.
3. For each eligible component, inspect its zero cells in the 8-neighbor perimeter. Recolor a zero 2 if it is exterior, or 3 if it is enclosed. Preserve other zeros and every original 1.
4. Check against examples: an open outline with no enclosed zero stays unchanged; for a qualifying outline, only 8-neighbor zeros around that outline change, using 2 outside and 3 inside. Verify dimensions and each row against the input.
